extracted.intended_audience: WGA members and participating screenwriters (and their representatives) involved in screen credit determinations and arbitrations
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, definitions, standards, and evidentiary guidelines used by the Writers Guild (WGA) to determine and arbitrate screenwriting credits under the MBA (Minimum Basic Agreement). Covers notice, protest, arbitration, credit categories, percentage thresholds, and related producer/production-executive rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Writer'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'writer' is defined in the MBA. In general, the term 'writer' means a person employed by a Company to write literary material or a person from whom a Company purchased literary material and who, at the time of purchase, was a 'professional writer,' as defined in the MBA. For purposes of credit, a team of writers ... is considered as one writer. If literary material covered under the MBA is written by one member of a team, separate and apart from the work of the team, such literary material shall be considered separate ... and such individual is eligible to receive writing credit as an individual writer and/or as a member of a team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who counts as a participating writer and how team-vs-individual contributions are treated for credit assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Professional Writer'
rubrics_metrics.description: The MBA generally defines a 'professional writer' as a person who has received employment for a total of thirteen weeks as a television or theatrical motion picture writer; or received credit on the screen for a television or theatrical motion picture; or received credit for a professionally produced play or a published novel. A writer may also negotiate with a Company to be treated as a 'professional writer' even if the writer would not otherwise qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines eligibility in certain situations (e.g., purchase from a non-member).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Literary Material'
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary material is written material and shall include stories, adaptations, treatments, original treatments, scenarios, continuities, teleplays, screenplays, dialogue, scripts, sketches, plots, outlines, narrative synopses, routines, and narrations, and, for use in the production of television film, formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes what documents are admissible evidence in credit determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Source Material'
rubrics_metrics.description: Source material is all material, other than story as hereinafter defined, upon which the story and/or screenplay is based. Source material is material assigned to the writer that was previously published or exploited and upon which the writer's work is to be based ... Not all assigned material is source material (e.g., literary material written by prior participating writers and research material are not considered source material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples of source credits wording and clarifies exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify other writers on assignment (Guild Working Rule 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer's responsibility begins at the moment the writer starts an assignment. Guild Working Rule 12 requires that the writer ascertain from the proper authorities in the production company the names of any other writers simultaneously assigned to the same material. The writer also must notify any such writers of the fact that the writer has been assigned to the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early notification preserves rights and helps avoid later disputes; Company also obligated to notify writers of other writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: File contract at Guild office promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member must promptly file a copy of the member’s contract of employment with the Guild, within one week after receipt of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts can be submitted electronically; filing helps verify dates/authorship during arbitration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep dated copies of all work submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: For fair credit determination, it is vital that writers keep copies of all work done. To be considered in a credit arbitration, literary material must have been submitted by the writer to the Company upon completion of the work or upon purchase. All material should be properly dated and labeled. Copies of story or script suggestions ... should be kept and must also have been submitted to the Company in writing if the writer wants to claim credit for these contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dated communications (e.g., emails) can place suggestions on the record; literature not submitted to Company is not admissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team of writers: definition and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'team' of writers is defined as two or more writers who collaborate to write a specific piece of literary material. The resulting literary material is attributable to the team as a whole, rather than to an individual member of the team. A waiver from the Guild is required for a team of more than three writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writers appear jointly, the work is presumed joint unless timely objection is made; team credit is denoted with an ampersand (&), and 'and' denotes separate, sequential authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration disputes should be raised contemporaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guild must presume that when two or more writers comply with the definition of a team and their names appear jointly on the work that is produced, the whole will be judged as a joint contribution unless a specific objection to this assumption is made at the time of the writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections should be made in writing to Credits staff and concurrently to the other writer; disputing collaboration months later is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for writing contract when team includes someone in additional capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: If a writer is employed to work as part of a team in collaboration with a writer also employed in an additional capacity (e.g., a producer or director), a writing contract for the team is required in order for the writer also employed in an additional capacity to claim co-authorship of the team's material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects against production-executive claims of co-authorship without appropriate contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of access to prior material
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the Guild that arbiters in credit arbitrations must assume that a writer has access to prior literary material verified for arbitration. This presumption that a writer has had access to prior literary material is irrebuttable, and a claim of writing independently of prior literary material may not be considered by a Policy Review Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access includes informal communications by producers, directors, executives; applied when significant similarity exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Tentative Writing Credits (Company obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theatrical Schedule A of our MBA provides that the Company will concurrently send to the Guild and to each participating writer ... a Notice of Tentative Writing Credits ('Notice'). The Company also is required to provide each participating writer ... a copy of the final shooting script (or if such script is not available, the latest revised script).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines participating writer; in remakes prior credited writers are participating writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to a Notice: agree, discuss, or protest
rubrics_metrics.description: 1) If a participating writer agrees with the tentative writing credits proposed by the Company, the writer does nothing. 2) If the writer wishes to discuss the credits with other participating writers, the writer may call the Guild to arrange discussion. 3) If the writer wishes to protest, the writer sends a written protest to both the Guild and the Company in substantially prescribed form, received within the time specified on the Notice (minimum MBA timelines apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No participating writer should request arbitration without first reading the final script; protest language form is provided in the Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for protest and arbitration initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests must be received by the Company and the Guild within the time specified at the bottom of the Notice, but in no event shall this time be less than that specified in the MBA ... (12 business days standard; emergency shortened to 7 business days possible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are strict; ensure contact info and representatives forward Notices promptly to avoid missing deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement among participating writers (pre-arbitration settlements)
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one writer has participated ... all participating writers have the right to agree unanimously among themselves as to which of them shall receive writing credits on the screen and in what form, provided that the form agreed upon is in accordance with Theatrical Schedule A of the MBA, and provided the agreement is reached in advance of arbitration. The MBA also provides that the form of such credit shall not be suggested or directed by the Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements should be confirmed in writing; Credits staff will attempt to facilitate meetings if a protest is received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration: selection of arbiters
rubrics_metrics.description: Any controversy as to credits shall be determined by an Arbitration Committee consisting of three members of the Guild who shall be drawn from the Screen Arbiters List. The Screen Arbiters List includes writers who have been current members for at least five years or who have received three screen credits. At least two of the three arbiters shall have served on no less than two previous Arbitration Committees. Participating writers may challenge a reasonable number of names; Credits staff selects arbiters from remaining names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wherever possible, arbiters experienced in the type of writing involved will be chosen; arbiters must have no interest in the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screen Credits Consultant role
rubrics_metrics.description: One member of the Guild's Screen Credits Committee shall be designated by Credits staff to act as Consultant for each Arbitration Committee, and during the arbitration period the Consultant shall be available ... for information on policy, rules, precedent, and procedure. It is the Consultant’s duty to aid the Committee in their effort to reach a majority decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultant advises on policy but is separate from arbiters and remains anonymous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity of arbiters, consultants, and writers' identities to Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of selected arbiters and consultants remain anonymous and confidential. The names of participating writers on the production shall not be revealed to the Arbitration Committee. Writers will be identified to the Arbitration Committee only as 'Writer A,' 'Writer B,' etc., reflecting the order in which the participating writers wrote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity is strict; statements and identities are not provided to other participants or the Company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant obligations: cooperate and verify
rubrics_metrics.description: All participating writers are obligated to cooperate with the Guild, including Credits staff, the Consultant, the Special Committee in a Pre-Arbitration, the Arbitration Committee, and the Policy Review Board panel, in every way required to render a fair and timely decision. The participating writer owes it to himself/herself to examine all literary material and source material submitted to the Guild by the Company and to make certain that all material written by the writer has been submitted and is accurately attributed and dated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May require an in-person review at Guild office; ensure full and accurate submission of authored material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of materials and cutting continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: The MBA requires the Company to submit three copies of all available material written by the participating writers as well as all available source material. Under provisions of the MBA, the Guild has the right to ask for a cutting continuity, which will be provided by the Company if it is available at the time of the arbitration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cutting continuity is submitted it is for reference (not credited to any writer); if not available, arbitration proceeds on final shooting script as submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a statement to the Arbitration Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement provides the participating writer an opportunity to explain why the writer is entitled to a particular credit. The statement should objectively and substantively address the requirements to receive credit as set forth in this Manual, 'Section III. Guild Policy on Credits.' The focus should be how the literary material has met the criteria outlined in the Manual for the credit the writer is seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended length 1–5 pages; personal statements written by the participant are preferred; avoid statements by lawyers/agents/‘statement experts’; avoid long enumerations/grids; include illustrative comparisons between final shooting script and earlier work; statements are confidential; Credits staff will review and may redact to conform with guidelines; statements delivered within 72 hours from notification that materials have been submitted (extensions sometimes allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited content in writers' statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that cannot be included in a writer’s statement includes, but is not limited to: entitlement to contingent compensation tied to receipt of credit; letters or comments of support from other individuals; development process information not germane to analysis; information revealing writer identities or prior credits; information contradicting Special Committee decisions; material not otherwise admissible; information about prior proceedings (hearings, arbitrations, expert readings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credits staff enforces compliance; non-compliant statements must be revised before submission to arbiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Arbitration Special Committee hearing (authenticity/classification/etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a dispute over the authenticity, classification, sequence, authorship, or completeness of any literary material to be considered in a credit arbitration, a Special Committee consisting of three members ... shall conduct a hearing at which all participating writers may present testimony and documentary evidence. This Special Committee is empowered to make a binding determination for purposes of submission of material to the arbiters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues include whether material was properly submitted, whether meets test of literary material vs research/producer's notes, correct dating/sequence, correct authorship identification, and completeness of submitted material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration Committee procedure and decision basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member of the Arbitration Committee reads all the submitted material independent of the other two arbiters and makes a decision based on the guidelines for determining credits. The Arbitration Committee bases its decision solely on literary and source material submitted for the arbitration. Members phone in their determination, seek unanimous agreement via teleconference facilitated by the Consultant; if unanimous decision cannot be reached, a majority decision prevails. Each member must confirm decision in writing with a summation of reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must be based on what material was actually used in final shooting script, not personal preference. The Credits staff communicates the final decision to interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Policy Review Board: strict 24-hour window and limited grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Within twenty-four hours of the initial notification of the Arbitration Committee's decision, any participating writer may request an appeal to a Policy Review Board. The Policy Review Board determines whether there has been any serious deviation from Guild policy or procedure. The Policy Review Board is not permitted to read the material involved for independently judging contributions and is not empowered to reverse judgments of relative contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only grounds for appeal: (a) dereliction of duty by Arbitration Committee member(s); (b) undue influence upon Arbitration Committee; (c) misinterpretation, misapplication, or violation of Guild policy; (d) availability of important literary or source material not previously available. Requestors may obtain arbiters' written summaries (without identities) and should submit a written statement outlining grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Credits staff member administering the arbitration shall write a letter to the Company and the participating writers notifying them of the final decision of the Arbitration Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This triggers the 24-hour appeal window and other post-decision processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of Guild decision and waiver of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Theatrical Schedule A provides: 'The decision of the Guild Arbitration Committee, and any Policy Review Board established by the Guild in connection therewith, with respect to writing credits, insofar as it is rendered within the limitations of this Schedule A, shall be final, and the Company will accept and follow the designation of screen credits contained in such decision and all writers shall be bound thereby.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers and companies waive rights to damages or injunctive relief as a result of such decisions; Guild may publish decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching rule: credit based on material in final shooting script
rubrics_metrics.description: Credit is determined by the material contributed to the final shooting script (as represented on the screen), rather than by the Arbitration Committee's personal preference of one script over another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses arbiters on textual/literary evidence connecting contributions to what appears on screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Written by' credit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Written by' is used when the writer(s) is entitled to both the 'Story by' credit and the 'Screenplay by' credit. This credit shall not be granted where there is source material of a story nature. ... 'Written by' credit generally will not be shared by more than two writers. In unusual cases ... the names of three writers or the names of writers constituting three writing teams may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies mainly to feature-length photoplays; limitations differ for episodic pictures and revues.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Story by' credit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'story' means all writing covered by the provisions of the MBA representing a contribution 'distinct from screenplay and consisting of basic narrative, idea, theme or outline indicating character development and action.' It is appropriate to award a 'Story by' credit when: 1) the story was written under employment under Guild jurisdiction; 2) the story was purchased by a signatory company from a professional writer; or 3) when the screenplay is based upon a sequel story written under the Guild's jurisdiction. Story credit may not be shared by more than two writers. Irreducible Shared Story Minimum: In the case of an original screenplay, the first writer shall be entitled to no less than a shared story credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes story elements from screenplay elements; arbiters must separate story contributions from screenplay contributions even when only a screenplay document is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Screen Story by' credit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If the writer is furnished source material of a story nature but takes from it only a springboard, a characterization, an incident, or some equally limited contribution, creating a substantially new and different story from the source material, the writer may receive 'Screen Story by' credit, but only as the result of arbitration. There is no percentage requirement to receive this credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source author may receive credit specifying form of acquisition (e.g., 'From a Novel by'); 'Screen Story' credit limited to two writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Screenplay by' credit rules and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A screenplay consists of individual scenes and full dialogue, together with such prior treatment, basic adaptation, continuity, scenario, and dialogue as shall be used in, and represent substantial contributions to the final script. A 'Screenplay by' credit is appropriate when there is source material of a story nature (with or without a screenplay) and when contribution meets the screenplay elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arbiters must consider dramatic construction, original/different scenes, characterization/relationships, and dialogue when assessing screenplay contribution; not determined by simply counting lines/pages—impact matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: selection from source material
rubrics_metrics.description: As a guideline for arbiters in cases involving a non-original screenplay based upon source material, ... selection of screenplay elements from the source material is a part of the creative process. Arbiters should give weight to any writer's original and unique utilization, choice, or arrangement of source material when it is present in the final shooting script, but not the employment of basic story elements that any other writer may have also selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes 'screenplay elements' (weighty) from 'story elements' (more basic); arbiters should read source material and all submissions to assess unique utilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional guidelines for arbiters assessing screenplay contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage contribution made by writers to screenplay obviously cannot be determined by counting lines or even the number of pages to which a writer has contributed. Arbiters must take into consideration the following elements ...: dramatic construction; original and different scenes; characterization or character relationships; and dialogue. It is up to the arbiters to determine which of the above-listed elements are most important to the overall values of the final screenplay in each particular case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small changes may or may not be significant—the impact on the whole script is the key factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Adaptation by' credit policy
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interest of avoiding a multiplicity of credits, the Guild is opposed to the general use of the 'Adaptation by' credit. However, the Guild recognizes that there are certain unusual cases where credit is due a writer who shapes the direction of screenplay construction without qualifying for 'Screenplay by' credit. In those special cases, and only as a result of arbitration, the 'Adaptation by' credit may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rare and only by arbitration.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Narration Written by' credit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Narration Written by' credit is appropriate where the major writing contribution to a motion picture is in the form of narration. The term 'narration' means material (typically off-camera) to explain or relate sequence or action (excluding promos or trailers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when narration is the major writing contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Additional Literary Material' credit
rubrics_metrics.description: All participating writers on a motion picture who are not accorded writing credit in accordance with Paragraphs 1–6 of Section III.A. of this Manual shall be entitled to receive credit in the form 'Additional Literary Material.' The names of the writers entitled to such credit shall be listed in alphabetical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default credit category for writers who contributed but did not meet thresholds for specific credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Based on Characters Created by' credit
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Based on Characters Created by' is a writing credit given to the writer(s) entitled to separated rights in a theatrical or television motion picture on each theatrical sequel to such theatrical or television motion picture. Where there are no separated rights, it may be accorded to the author of source material upon which a sequel is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to sequels and separated rights contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: No other credits approved without waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Any form of credit not expressly described in this Manual shall be used only upon receipt of a waiver from the Guild.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts proliferation of novel credit types to protect value of credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production executives: definition and special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'production executives' ... individuals who receive credit either as a producer in any capacity, or as the director. Writers should be aware that receiving any form of producing or directing credit qualifies them as a production executive for the purpose of arbitration. The Guild will not consider the basis upon which the credit was granted for the purpose of determining that a writer receiving credit as a production executive should not be subject to the rules for production executives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production-executive status triggers automatic arbitration in many circumstances and imposes different percentage burdens to obtain screenplay credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production executives: notice and teaming requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a production executive intends to claim credit as a team on any literary material with a writer(s) who is not a production executive, the production executive must, at the time when such team writing begins, have signified such claim in writing to the Guild and to the writer(s) with whom the production executive claims to have worked as a team. Failure to comply will preclude such production executive from claiming co-authorship of the literary material in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects other writers from retroactive production-executive claims of co-authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production executive percentage requirements for screenplay credit
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of the credit arbitration, the production executive or production executive team must assume the burden of proving that ... they had, in fact, worked on the script as a writer and had assumed full share of the writing. In the case of an original screenplay, if the production executive or production executive team is not the first writer, the production executive or production executive team must have contributed more than 50% of the final script to receive screenplay credit. In the case of a non-original screenplay, the production executive or production executive team must have contributed more than 33% to receive screenplay credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contribution must consist of dramatic construction, original/different scenes, characterization/relationships, and dialogue; keep dated copies of all literary material submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remake rules for prior writers
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of remakes, any writer who has received writing credit under the Guild's jurisdiction in connection with a prior version of the motion picture is a participating writer on the remake. Those prior writers are entitled to participate and are eligible to receive writing credit pursuant to the rules. The final shooting script written by a prior writer(s) shall be considered literary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arbitration may award no credit, a 'based on' credit only, writing credit only (no more than original), or both writing and 'based on' credit. Remakes are considered non-original screenplays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from credit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A participating writer may not withdraw from credit on a motion picture on which the writer is the only participating writer. Prior to the time a credit question has been submitted to arbitration, a writer may withdraw from screenwriting credit for personal cause. After screen credits have been determined by arbitration, a writer may not withdraw from writing credit. Withdrawal from writing credit will result in loss of any and all rights accruing from receipt of writing credit. Use of a pseudonym rather than withdrawing from credit will not result in such a forfeiture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal must be timely and may be subject to arbitration if other contributors disagree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guild's right to protest company-proposed credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the provisions of the MBA the Guild has the right to protest credits proposed by the Company. The Guild may act irrespective of the wishes of any of the participating writers in order to ensure that the credit rules are properly applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guild can initiate automatic arbitrations per MBA provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of names in shared credits
rubrics_metrics.description: The order of writers' names in a shared credit may be arbitrated. Generally, the most substantial contributor overall is entitled to first position credit, although the ultimate determination is within the sole discretion of the Arbitration Committee. Where there is no agreement among the arbiters as to order of names, or where the Arbitration Committee determines that the credited writers' contributions are equal, then the Arbitration Committee shall order the writers' names chronologically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chronological order used when contributions are equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudonym rules for screen credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any writer who is entitled to credit on the screen and who has been paid (or is guaranteed payment of) less than two hundred thousand dollars ($200,000) for writing services ... shall have the right to be accorded credit on the screen ... in a reasonable pseudonymous name. A writer must exercise this right within five (5) business days after final determination of writing credits. Before using a pseudonym a writer must register it with the Guild ... A pseudonym may not duplicate the name or pseudonym of another writer or the name of a public figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credits staff may obtain the true name/identity of pseudonymous writers under certain conditions; refusal to reveal true identity in some cases may preclude pseudonymous writer from receiving credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written material prevails over statements or extraneous evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of Arbitration Committees are based solely upon literary and source material. A writer’s written statement to the Arbitration Committee is not a basis for an award of writing credit. Claims of authorship must be supported by literary material appropriate for submission to the Arbitration Committee. In the event of conflicting claims, literary material always prevails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes documentary evidence—scripts, treatments, etc.—over testimony, publicity, or contractual incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening credits after revision of script
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after screen credits are finally determined, material changes are made in the literary material, either the Company or a participating writer and the Guild jointly may reopen credit determination by making a claim within 48 hours after completion of the writing work claimed to justify the revision of credits; and in such case the procedure for the original determination of credits is followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short 48-hour window after claimed new writing work completion—act promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicizing credits and confidentiality expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a violation of the MBA and Guild Working Rules for a writer to claim credit for screen authorship on any motion picture prior to the time when the credits have been determined and for a writer to claim credits contrary to such final determination. The Guild asks participating writers to refrain from commenting in the press, media, or on social media about issues related to pre-arbitration hearings, arbiters' written decisions, or Policy Review Board hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations can result in disciplinary action; confidentiality protects integrity of process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guild discretion and ability to depart from precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: These rules and procedures have been derived from the experience and practice of the past years. Although they remain the guiding policy by which credits are determined, they are not to be considered rigid or inflexible. The Guild has the discretion to depart from precedent when new conditions, new problems, or new methods of work may require an alteration of the rules or a new application of an existing rule to a unique set of facts and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arbiters and Credits staff may exercise judgment in novel situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A: Percentage requirements to receive screenplay credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Chart summarizing percentage requirements to receive screenplay credit (based on final shooting script). First Writer – Non Production Executive: >33% (Original & Non-Original). First Writer – Production Executive or P.E. Team: >33% (Original & Non-Original). Subsequent Writer – Non Production Executive: 50% (Original), >33% (Non-Original). Subsequent Writer – Production Executive or P.E. Team: >50% (Original), >33% (Non-Original).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These percentage thresholds are guidelines for arbiters to determine entitlement to 'Screenplay by' credit; percentages cannot be mechanically calculated—impact and element importance matter.
